questions.question: How many bits are in a nibble and a byte?
questions.answer: A nibble has 4 bits and a byte has 8 bits.
questions.explanation: A nibble has 4 bits and a byte has 8 bits.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) What is the IDE run-time environment for? (2) What does a translator integrated into an IDE provide?
options: Back up only; cannot execute / Compile or interpret for execution
Run/test and inspect output / Turn RAM into permanent storage
Back up only; cannot execute / Turn RAM into permanent storage
Run/test and inspect output / Compile or interpret for execution
questions.answer: D — Run/test and inspect output / Compile or interpret for execution
questions.explanation: (1) Running and testing a program and inspecting its behaviour or output. (2) Compilation or interpretation so source code can be executed as machine instructions.

questions.question: How do IDE error diagnostics help?
questions.answer: They show errors and often their location, helping the programmer find the cause.
questions.explanation: They show errors and often their location, helping the programmer find the cause.

questions.question: Two computers receive the same byte but show different characters. Why? What must match?
questions.answer: The computers use different character sets or encodings. To show the same letter, both need a matching encoding.
questions.explanation: The computers use different character sets or encodings. To show the same letter, both need a matching encoding.

questions.question: Convert 00101101 binary to denary.
Two computers need to interpret stored text codes consistently. What is a character set?
options: A defined collection of characters with corresponding codes.
The collection of fonts available for displaying one character.
The number of pixels used to draw a character on a screen.
The list of filenames stored on a drive.
questions.answer: A — A defined collection of characters with corresponding codes.
questions.explanation: A defined collection of characters with corresponding codes.

questions.question: “A record must contain only one unnamed value.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Named fields about one item or person. Fields may have different data types.
questions.explanation: Named fields about one item or person. Fields may have different data types.

questions.question: Valid ages are 13–18. Changing <18 to <=18 fixes a bug. Give three tests near 18 and their expected results. Why retest a value that worked before?
questions.answer: 17 accepted; 18 accepted; 19 rejected. Retest a value that worked before to check for regression: a new fault caused by the fix.
questions.explanation: 17 accepted; 18 accepted; 19 rejected. Retest a value that worked before to check for regression: a new fault caused by the fix.

questions.question: Why does 11111111 plus 00000001 overflow eight bits?
questions.answer: The true sum is 256, requiring nine bits; only eight stored bits would contain 00000000.
questions.explanation: The true sum is 256, requiring nine bits; only eight stored bits would contain 00000000.

questions.question: Given A has code 65 and capital-letter codes are consecutive, give the code for D and explain how you found it.
options: 68; D is 3 position(s) after A.
questions.answer: B — 68; D is 3 position(s) after A.
questions.explanation: 68; D is 3 position(s) after A.
prerequisite_notes: Explicitly model adjacent-code inference with supplied codes; do not ask pupils to memorise ASCII values.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: “Unicode supports fewer characters than standard ASCII.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Unicode supports far more characters than standard ASCII.
questions.explanation: Unicode supports far more characters than standard ASCII.

questions.question: A program calculates an area and shows a menu in several places. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) A function cannot return a value. (b) A procedure must return a value.
questions.answer: (a) A function returns a value, such as an area. (b) A procedure performs a task, such as showing a menu, without returning a value. Use arguments and return values to avoid unwanted changes to global data.
questions.explanation: (a) A function returns a value, such as an area. (b) A procedure performs a task, such as showing a menu, without returning a value. Use arguments and return values to avoid unwanted changes to global data.

questions.question: Convert hexadecimal A3 to eight-bit binary.
A character code uses exactly 7 bits. How many different characters can it represent? Can it encode 129 different characters without more bits?
options: 128 characters; yes.
14 characters; no.
2^7 = 128; no, one more character requires more distinct codes.
7 characters; yes.
questions.answer: C — 2^7 = 128; no, one more character requires more distinct codes.
questions.explanation: 2^7 = 128; no, one more character requires more distinct codes.
prerequisite_notes: Model 2^n character capacity; present Unicode as variable encoding, not one fixed number of bits.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: “Metadata is another name for the colour of every pixel.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Extra image details, such as width, height or colour depth. These are separate from pixel data.
questions.explanation: Extra image details, such as width, height or colour depth. These are separate from pixel data.

questions.question: (a) A bitmap uses 5 bits per pixel. How many colours can it show? What if you add one bit? (b) A 50 × 20 pixel image doubles in width and height. Colour depth stays the same. How do pixel count and raw size change? Explain.
questions.answer: (a) 32 colours; one extra bit doubles this to 64. (b) 1,000 pixels become 4,000. Raw size is four times larger: both dimensions double.
questions.explanation: (a) 32 colours; one extra bit doubles this to 64. (b) 1,000 pixels become 4,000. Raw size is four times larger: both dimensions double.
topics: Colour-depth quality size and colour count

questions.question: How does a bitmap represent pixel colours?
questions.answer: Each pixel has a colour code stored in binary.
questions.explanation: Each pixel has a colour code stored in binary.

questions.question: Several apps use lots of RAM. Data often moves between RAM and an SSD. Why can heavy virtual-memory use reduce performance?
options: Secondary storage always provides faster access than RAM.
Using more storage capacity automatically doubles CPU clock speed.
Transfers to secondary storage eliminate every memory-access delay.
Data must be transferred between RAM and slower secondary storage, increasing access delays.
questions.answer: D — Data must be transferred between RAM and slower secondary storage, increasing access delays.
questions.explanation: Data must be transferred between RAM and slower secondary storage, increasing access delays.

questions.question: “A parameter is the final printed output of every program.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.
questions.explanation: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.

questions.question: A microphone records digital sound. “Sampling stores every instant of the sound wave.” Correct this. How does it affect recorded detail?
questions.answer: Measure amplitude at regular intervals. Store each rounded (quantised) value in binary. Sample rate and bit depth limit the detail captured.
questions.explanation: Measure amplitude at regular intervals. Store each rounded (quantised) value in binary. Sample rate and bit depth limit the detail captured.

questions.question: What does lossy compression do?
questions.answer: It discards some information, so the exact original cannot necessarily be restored.
questions.explanation: It discards some information, so the exact original cannot necessarily be restored.

questions.question: An image has not been saved. What does RAM hold while a program is running?
options: The program's active instructions and working data.
Only permanent startup firmware that cannot change during use.
Only files that have already been saved for long-term archiving.
Only the address of the next instruction in the CPU.
questions.answer: A — The program's active instructions and working data.
questions.explanation: The program's active instructions and working data.

questions.question: “Sample rate is the number of bits used for each sample.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Sample rate is samples per second. At 8,000 Hz, 8,000 samples are taken each second. A higher rate can capture more detail but uses more space.
questions.explanation: Sample rate is samples per second. At 8,000 Hz, 8,000 samples are taken each second. A higher rate can capture more detail but uses more space.

questions.question: Two recordings have the same sample rate and length but different bit depths. “Bit depth is samples per second.” Correct this. How does bit depth affect detail and size?
questions.answer: Bit depth is bits per sample. More bits allow more amplitude levels but use more space. Longer duration adds samples; sample rate and bit depth control detail.
questions.explanation: Bit depth is bits per sample. More bits allow more amplitude levels but use more space. Longer duration adds samples; sample rate and bit depth control detail.

questions.question: What is abstraction?
questions.answer: Removing irrelevant detail while keeping what is needed to solve the problem.
questions.explanation: Removing irrelevant detail while keeping what is needed to solve the problem.

questions.question: A query should return pupils whose mark is at least 70. What does WHERE do in an SQL query?
options: It automatically sorts the result without any comparison condition.
It selects rows that meet a condition.
It selects which output columns appear, but never filters rows.
It identifies the source table, but never tests a condition.
questions.answer: B — It selects rows that meet a condition.
questions.explanation: It selects rows that meet a condition.

questions.question: A zero-indexed 2D array is [[11,12],[21,22]]. Give grid[1,0], then state the indexes needed to access 12.
questions.answer: grid[1,0] is 21; 12 is at grid[0,1].
questions.explanation: grid[1,0] is 21; 12 is at grid[0,1].

questions.question: Two mono recordings have the same sample rate and bit depth. One lasts twice as long. Does this double its quality? How does raw size change?
questions.answer: Raw size doubles: there are twice as many samples. Quality does not improve. Sample rate and bit depth stay the same.
questions.explanation: Raw size doubles: there are twice as many samples. Quality does not improve. Sample rate and bit depth stay the same.
topics: Duration effect on size versus quality

questions.question: What does a diamond represent in a flowchart?
questions.answer: A decision or condition with alternative paths.
questions.explanation: A decision or condition with alternative paths.

questions.question: A game simulates a six-sided die. Which integers can random(1,6) produce in OCR ERL?
options: Only 0 through 5 inclusive.
Only 1 through 5, because the upper endpoint is excluded.
Any integer from 1 through 6 inclusive.
Only integers 2 through 5, excluding both endpoints.
questions.answer: C — Any integer from 1 through 6 inclusive.
questions.explanation: Any integer from 1 through 6 inclusive.
topics: Generate and use bounded random integers

questions.question: “A USB flash drive stores data on a rotating magnetic platter.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Solid-state storage with no moving read/write mechanism.
questions.explanation: Solid-state storage with no moving read/write mechanism.

questions.question: A large file must cross a slow link. “Compression always makes files larger.” Correct this. How might compression affect transfer time?
questions.answer: A smaller file uses less storage and can be sent faster over the same link. Compression and decompression take processing time.
questions.explanation: A smaller file uses less storage and can be sent faster over the same link. Compression and decompression take processing time.

questions.question: Why must a trace table follow executed assignments in order?
questions.answer: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.
questions.explanation: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.

questions.question: A website thumbnail may tolerate a small reduction in detail. What does lossy compression do?
options: It guarantees exact reconstruction of all original information.
It changes data into ciphertext while preserving every original detail.
It stores a duplicate of every original byte with no removed information.
It discards some information, so the exact original cannot necessarily be restored.
questions.answer: D — It discards some information, so the exact original cannot necessarily be restored.
questions.explanation: It discards some information, so the exact original cannot necessarily be restored.

questions.question: “Changing a variable name automatically fixes every logic error.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Clear names show what values mean and help people read and change code.
questions.explanation: Clear names show what values mean and help people read and change code.

questions.question: A program is compressed before being sent. “Lossless compression removes source-code characters.” Correct this. Why does it matter here?
questions.answer: Lossless compression restores every character exactly. Losing characters could break the program. A thumbnail can lose some detail; source code cannot.
questions.explanation: Lossless compression restores every character exactly. Losing characters could break the program. A thumbnail can lose some detail; source code cannot.

questions.question: Does linear search require a sorted list?
questions.answer: No; it examines items in sequence until a match is found or the list ends.
questions.explanation: No; it examines items in sequence until a match is found or the list ends.

questions.question: A quiz application needs scoring, questions, input handling and a menu. What is decomposition?
options: Breaking a complex problem into smaller manageable subproblems.
Remove irrelevant details but never split the task into parts.
Choose a programming language before identifying any subproblem.
Put every requirement into one unstructured instruction.
questions.answer: A — Breaking a complex problem into smaller manageable subproblems.
questions.explanation: Breaking a complex problem into smaller manageable subproblems.

questions.question: “Every local variable can always be accessed directly from every other subprogram.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A local variable can be used only within its own subprogram or local scope.
questions.explanation: A local variable can be used only within its own subprogram or local scope.
prerequisite_notes: Include local constants as well as local variables.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: Several procedures share a global score. “A global variable can be read only in one subprogram.” Correct this. What risk does sharing it create?
questions.answer: Global variables can be used across the program. This risks unwanted changes and makes faults harder to trace. Use arguments and return values to avoid hidden changes.
questions.explanation: Global variables can be used across the program. This risks unwanted changes and makes faults harder to trace. Use arguments and return values to avoid hidden changes.
prerequisite_notes: Include global constants as well as global variables.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: What must be true before binary search is used?
questions.answer: The list must be sorted. This lets the search safely rule out half the remaining items.
questions.explanation: The list must be sorted. This lets the search safely rule out half the remaining items.
topics: Binary search steps precondition and trace

questions.question: A CPU needs to access memory location 120. What does the MAR hold?
options: The address of the next instruction, regardless of the location being accessed.
The address of the memory location being accessed.
The data transferred from the selected memory location.
The result of the most recent calculation.
questions.answer: B — The address of the memory location being accessed.
questions.explanation: The address of the memory location being accessed.

questions.question: “Functions can return only one digit and can never return an array.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Yes. A subprogram can receive an array; a function can return an array.
questions.explanation: Yes. A subprogram can receive an array; a function can return an array.
prerequisite_notes: Verify both passing AND returning an array; an array parameter alone is insufficient.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: A café program finds the cost of identical drinks. “Inputs are the final results.” Correct this. Give the inputs, process and output.
questions.answer: Inputs: price and quantity. Processing: multiply them. Output: total cost. Inputs come before the calculation; the output comes after it.
questions.explanation: Inputs: price and quantity. Processing: multiply them. Output: total cost. Inputs come before the calculation; the output comes after it.

questions.question: When does ascending bubble sort swap two adjacent items?
questions.answer: When the left item is greater than the right item.
questions.explanation: When the left item is greater than the right item.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) What does readLine() do on an opened text file? (2) What does writeLine(text) do?
options: Read next text line / Only display on screen
Write a new line / Only display on screen
Read next text line / Write text to file
Write a new line / Write text to file
questions.answer: C — Read next text line / Write text to file
questions.explanation: (1) It reads the next line and advances the current position. (2) It writes the supplied text as a line through an opened file handle.

questions.question: “Primary storage exists only to keep long-term backups.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It holds instructions and working data that the CPU needs while programs run.
questions.explanation: It holds instructions and working data that the CPU needs while programs run.

questions.question: “My unsaved work will survive a power cut because this computer has ROM.” Explain the mistake. How could the work have been kept?
questions.answer: Unsaved work is in volatile RAM, so it is lost when power goes off. Save it to non-volatile secondary storage to keep it.
questions.explanation: Unsaved work is in volatile RAM, so it is lost when power goes off. Save it to non-volatile secondary storage to keep it.

questions.question: What does insertion sort do with the next unsorted item?
questions.answer: Place the next item in the correct position in the sorted part. Shift larger items right.
questions.explanation: Place the next item in the correct position in the sorted part. Shift larger items right.

questions.question: A computer needs startup instructions when switched on. What is ROM usually used for?
options: Temporary working values lost at shutdown.
The entire changing contents of every running application.
Only the latest numerical result held by the ALU.
Retaining firmware or startup instructions when power is off.
questions.answer: D — Retaining firmware or startup instructions when power is off.
questions.explanation: Retaining firmware or startup instructions when power is off.

questions.question: “Cache is a remote Internet server that replaces CPU registers.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Cache is in or near the CPU. It gives faster access to often-used data and instructions than main memory.
questions.explanation: Cache is in or near the CPU. It gives faster access to often-used data and instructions than main memory.

questions.question: A pupil restarts a computer to open saved work. “RAM keeps every file forever.” Correct this. Why is secondary storage needed?
questions.answer: Secondary storage keeps files and programs without power. Save the work there before restarting.
questions.explanation: Secondary storage keeps files and programs without power. Save the work there before restarting.

questions.lesson_title: GCSE Synoptic Revision: Paper 1 and Paper 2 (exception lesson)
questions.question: How does merge sort combine two sorted lists?
questions.answer: Compare the next item in each list. Take the smaller. Repeat, then add any items left over.
questions.explanation: Compare the next item in each list. Take the smaller. Repeat, then add any items left over.

questions.lesson_title: GCSE Synoptic Revision: Paper 1 and Paper 2 (exception lesson)
questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) Which storage technology does a DVD use? (2) Which storage technology does a hard disk drive use?
options: Laser-based optical storage / Magnetic rotating platters
Magnetic flash storage / Magnetic rotating platters
Laser-based optical storage / No moving parts, only flash chips
Magnetic flash storage / No moving parts, only flash chips
questions.answer: A — Laser-based optical storage / Magnetic rotating platters
questions.explanation: (1) Optical storage, read using laser light. (2) Magnetic storage on rotating platters.

questions.lesson_title: GCSE Synoptic Revision: Paper 1 and Paper 2 (exception lesson)
questions.question: “FROM is the clause that specifies the required output columns.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: The table to get data from.
questions.explanation: The table to get data from.

questions.lesson_title: GCSE Synoptic Revision: Paper 1 and Paper 2 (exception lesson)
questions.question: Code has a missing bracket. “A syntax error is a wrong result from code that follows the language's rules.” Correct this. What needs fixing?
questions.answer: A syntax error breaks the language's rules and stops the affected code being translated or run. Fix it, then trace and test the logic.
questions.explanation: A syntax error breaks the language's rules and stops the affected code being translated or run. Fix it, then trace and test the logic.

questions.question: Which CPU component performs arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.answer: The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.
questions.explanation: The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) Why might an HDD suit a large stationary archive? (2) Does no moving parts mean a storage device cannot fail?
options: Cheapest always best in every respect / SSD cannot fail; no backup needed
Capacity and cost per GB trade-off / All devices can fail; retain backups
Cheapest always best in every respect / All devices can fail; retain backups
Capacity and cost per GB trade-off / SSD cannot fail; no backup needed
questions.answer: B — Capacity and cost per GB trade-off / All devices can fail; retain backups
questions.explanation: (1) It can provide high capacity at a relatively low cost per GB; the choice depends on current devices and requirements. (2) No; electronic faults, wear and other failures remain possible, so backups are still needed.

questions.question: “An SSD is faster because its magnetic read head rotates more quickly.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It does not need a moving head to seek positions on spinning platters.
questions.explanation: It does not need a moving head to seek positions on spinning platters.

questions.question: A laptop is used on a bumpy bus. “Portability and durability mean the same thing.” Correct this. How should this affect the storage choice?
questions.answer: Durability means resisting damage; portability means being easy to carry. An SSD has no moving read/write parts, so it handles shocks better. Size and weight also matter.
questions.explanation: Durability means resisting damage; portability means being easy to carry. An SSD has no moving read/write parts, so it handles shocks better. Size and weight also matter.

questions.question: For s = 'COMPUTER', what is s.substring(1,3) in OCR ERL?
questions.answer: OMP; indexing starts at zero and the second argument gives length.
questions.explanation: OMP; indexing starts at zero and the second argument gives length.

questions.question: A program reads a name and displays a greeting. What is the difference between input and output?
options: Input and output both mean the intermediate multiplication step.
Output is information entered by the user, while input is the printed response.
Input enters a program; output is information the program produces.
Input is only the final displayed result; output is only a keyboard entry.
questions.answer: C — Input enters a program; output is information the program produces.
questions.explanation: Input enters a program; output is information the program produces.

questions.question: “Duplicating the same long code block everywhere always improves maintainability.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Related logic can be reused, understood, tested and changed in one place.
questions.explanation: Related logic can be reused, understood, tested and changed in one place.

questions.question: Nested IF statements are hard to read. “Indentation proves the logic is correct.” Correct this. How does indentation help?
questions.answer: Indentation shows blocks and nesting. Some languages require it. It helps people read and change code, but does not prove the logic is correct.
questions.explanation: Indentation shows blocks and nesting. Some languages require it. It helps people read and change code, but does not prove the logic is correct.

questions.question: How is a cell selected in a two-dimensional array?
questions.answer: Use two indexes: one for the row and one for the column.
questions.explanation: Use two indexes: one for the row and one for the column.

questions.question: A non-obvious validation rule needs to be maintained next year. What makes a useful code comment?
options: Repeat misleading old instructions even after the code changes.
Describe the opposite of the implemented validation rule.
Replace executable statements because comments calculate the result.
It explains important intent or reasoning without misleading the reader.
questions.answer: D — It explains important intent or reasoning without misleading the reader.
questions.explanation: It explains important intent or reasoning without misleading the reader.

questions.question: “The CPU's main purpose is permanent file storage.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It executes instructions to process data.
questions.explanation: It executes instructions to process data.

questions.question: A folder contains 20 images of 200 KB each. Using decimal units, give its total size in KB and MB.
prerequisite_notes: Add a worked multiple-file capacity example before retrieval.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: What is the scope of a local variable or constant?
questions.answer: A local variable can be used only within its own subprogram or local scope.
questions.explanation: A local variable can be used only within its own subprogram or local scope.
prerequisite_notes: Include local constants as well as local variables.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) What happens during the fetch stage? (2) What happens during the decode stage?
options: Obtain next instruction from memory / Interpret the fetched instruction
Carry out its calculation / Interpret the fetched instruction
Obtain next instruction from memory / Save all source code permanently
Carry out its calculation / Save all source code permanently
questions.answer: A — Obtain next instruction from memory / Interpret the fetched instruction
questions.explanation: (1) The next instruction is obtained from memory. (2) The instruction is interpreted so the required operation can be identified.

questions.question: “Execution only copies an instruction into memory without performing it.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: The operation specified by the decoded instruction is carried out.
questions.explanation: The operation specified by the decoded instruction is carried out.

questions.question: “The Control Unit stores your documents forever.” Correct this. Explain its role when the CPU runs an instruction.
questions.answer: The Control Unit decodes instructions and controls CPU operations. The ALU processes data; registers store it briefly.
questions.explanation: The Control Unit decodes instructions and controls CPU operations. The ALU processes data; registers store it briefly.

questions.question: Why open a file before reading it?
questions.answer: Opening establishes a handle or connection through which the program accesses the file.
questions.explanation: Opening establishes a handle or connection through which the program accesses the file.

questions.question: A loop repeatedly uses the same instructions. What does CPU cache hold?
options: Only values arriving through a network cable.
Frequently or recently used data and instructions for rapid access.
Only the address of the next instruction.
Every user's complete archive after shutdown.
questions.answer: B — Frequently or recently used data and instructions for rapid access.
questions.explanation: Frequently or recently used data and instructions for rapid access.

questions.question: “A register is a large external drive used for backups.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A small, fast storage location inside the CPU. It holds data or addresses in use.
questions.explanation: A small, fast storage location inside the CPU. It holds data or addresses in use.
topics: Registers as small fast CPU storage

questions.question: The next instruction is at address 240. An addition gives 18. What do the accumulator and Program Counter hold? Explain the difference.
questions.answer: The accumulator holds the result, 18. The PC holds the next instruction's address, 240.
questions.explanation: The accumulator holds the result, 18. The PC holds the next instruction's address, 240.

questions.question: What does SELECT specify in an SQL query?
questions.answer: The fields (columns) to return.
questions.explanation: The fields (columns) to return.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) What does a higher clock speed mean? (2) When can additional CPU cores improve performance?
options: More clock cycles per second / Always doubles every program's speed
Guaranteed double speed for every task / Always doubles every program's speed
More clock cycles per second / Helps parallel or concurrent work
Guaranteed double speed for every task / Helps parallel or concurrent work
questions.answer: C — More clock cycles per second / Helps parallel or concurrent work
questions.explanation: (1) More CPU clock cycles occur each second; this can increase instruction throughput under comparable conditions. (2) When work can be distributed across cores, allowing more tasks or instruction streams to progress concurrently.

questions.question: “Larger cache increases the number of installed CPU cores.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A larger cache holds more often-used data and instructions. This can reduce slower memory access.
questions.explanation: A larger cache holds more often-used data and instructions. This can reduce slower memory access.

questions.question: CPU A: 4 GHz, two cores, 2 MB cache. CPU B: 3 GHz, eight cores, 8 MB cache. Why is neither fastest for every task?
questions.answer: A has more cycles per second, which may help one task. B has more cores for parallel work and more cache to reduce slow memory access. Speed also depends on the task and CPU design.
questions.explanation: A has more cycles per second, which may help one task. B has more cores for parallel work and more cache to reduce slow memory access. Speed also depends on the task and CPU design.

questions.question: Which integers can random(1,6) produce in OCR ERL?
questions.answer: Any integer from 1 through 6 inclusive.
questions.explanation: Any integer from 1 through 6 inclusive.
topics: Generate and use bounded random integers

questions.question: A programmer plans an age-checking algorithm before coding it. Why use pseudocode when designing an algorithm?
options: It must use valid binary machine instructions for one processor.
It can only describe how the interface looks, never processing.
It guarantees an incorrect algorithm becomes correct without testing.
Pseudocode shows steps in order without needing one programming language's exact syntax.
questions.answer: D — Pseudocode shows steps in order without needing one programming language's exact syntax.
questions.explanation: It expresses ordered algorithmic steps without requiring the exact syntax of one programming language.

questions.question: “A diamond is used only for unconditional calculations.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A decision or condition with alternative paths.
questions.explanation: A decision or condition with alternative paths.

questions.question: A program works out a bill, then applies a discount. “The order of steps never matters.” Correct this. What could go wrong?
questions.answer: Steps must be clear and in the right order. Check that conditions give the right result for every allowed input.
questions.explanation: Steps must be clear and in the right order. Check that conditions give the right result for every allowed input.

questions.question: In a trace table, should you record executed variable updates or only variable names?
questions.answer: Executed variable updates in their actual order.
questions.explanation: Executed variable updates in their actual order.

questions.question: A circuit must invert a sensor's signal. How can you recognise a NOT gate symbol?
options: It is a one-input inverter, usually a triangle with a small output bubble.
A two-input gate with a flat left edge and rounded right edge.
A two-input gate with a curved input edge and no inversion bubble.
A four-input gate that always leaves each input unchanged.
questions.answer: A — It is a one-input inverter, usually a triangle with a small output bubble.
questions.explanation: It is a one-input inverter, usually a triangle with a small output bubble.

questions.question: An indicator uses Q = NOT A. Give outputs for A=0 and A=1, then evaluate NOT(NOT A) for both values.
questions.answer: Q: 1, 0. Double NOT: 0, 1, restoring A.
questions.explanation: Q: 1, 0. Double NOT: 0, 1, restoring A.

questions.question: Linear-search [7, 2, 9, 4] for 2, starting at index 0. List the values checked. How many comparisons are needed?
questions.answer: (a) [7, 2]; 2 comparison(s), found at index 1.

[[3, 7, 6, 2], [3, 6, 7, 2], [3, 6, 2, 7]]; largest value 7 is at the right end.

questions.question: “An IF statement must execute every possible branch regardless of its condition.” Correct this. Explain why.

questions.question: What does authentication establish?
questions.answer: Whether a user has supplied suitable evidence of the claimed identity.
questions.explanation: Whether a user has supplied suitable evidence of the claimed identity.

questions.question: A CPU must execute a program written in a high-level language. Why is a translator needed for high-level source code?

It changes every algorithm into a flowchart without producing executable instructions.
A CPU runs machine instructions. High-level source code must be translated before or as it runs.
It only translates comments into another human language.

questions.question: “Sequence means the computer chooses any random instruction order.” Correct this. Explain why.

questions.question: What does anticipating misuse mean in defensive design?
questions.answer: Planning for invalid, unexpected or malicious use and handling it safely.
questions.explanation: Planning for invalid, unexpected or malicious use and handling it safely.

questions.question: Merge the sorted lists [1, 5] and [4, 6] into ascending order. Give the values in order. Why not just join the lists?
options: [1, 5, 4, 6]; concatenation is always sufficient.
[4, 6, 1, 5]; reversing list order always sorts.
[6, 5, 4, 1]; descending order is ascending.
[1, 4, 5, 6]. Repeatedly select the smaller next available value; concatenation would leave a larger left-list value before a smaller right-list value.
questions.answer: D — [1, 4, 5, 6]. Repeatedly select the smaller next available value; concatenation would leave a larger left-list value before a smaller right-list value.
questions.explanation: [1, 4, 5, 6]. Repeatedly select the smaller next available value; concatenation would leave a larger left-list value before a smaller right-list value.

questions.question: “A comparison operator must always produce a text paragraph.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A Boolean result: true or false.
questions.explanation: A Boolean result: true or false.

questions.question: A school shares files and printers on one site. “A LAN must span several countries.” Correct this. Why does a LAN fit here?
questions.answer: A LAN connects devices in a small area, such as one school site. A WAN links networks over a large area. Internet access alone does not make a LAN a WAN.
questions.explanation: A LAN connects devices in a small area, such as one school site. A WAN links networks over a large area. Internet access alone does not make a LAN a WAN.

questions.question: For valid ages 13–18, identify the two valid boundary values.
questions.answer: 13 and 18 lie on the edges of the valid range.
questions.explanation: 13 and 18 lie on the edges of the valid range.

questions.question: A pupil needs to change a line of source code. What is the IDE editor used for?
options: Writing and editing source code, often with helpful formatting or highlighting.
Repairing physical CPU faults.
Rearranging fragments on a magnetic hard disk.
Allocating user access rights in the operating system.

questions.explanation: Writing and editing source code, often with helpful formatting or highlighting.

questions.question: “The first index in every OCR ERL array is 1.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.
questions.explanation: A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.

questions.question: A ticket program checks ages. “A few successful tests prove it has no faults.” Correct this. How should it be tested?
questions.answer: Test valid and invalid inputs. Compare actual and expected results to find faults. A few successful tests cannot prove there are no faults.

questions.answer: Testing and correcting parts during development as the solution is built.

questions.question: A booking program is tested before release. “Final testing means no testing is needed while building it.” Correct this. Why are both needed?
questions.answer: Final testing checks the finished program against its requirements. Testing during development finds faults earlier. Both are needed.
questions.explanation: Final testing checks the finished program against its requirements. Testing during development finds faults earlier. Both are needed.

questions.question: What does the Program Counter hold?
questions.answer: The address of the next instruction to be fetched.
questions.explanation: The address of the next instruction to be fetched.

questions.question: Choose outputs for 00, 01, 10, 11: (1) Q = A AND B (interlock); (2) Q = A OR B (alarm). Which inputs allow the interlock to work? Does 11 trigger the alarm?
options: 0, 0, 0, 1 / 0, 1, 1, 0; simultaneous inputs cancel.

0, 1, 1, 1; any high input permits operation. / 0, 1, 1, 1

questions.question: “A NIC's purpose is keeping files when power is off.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: The interface that enables a device to connect to a network.
questions.explanation: The interface that enables a device to connect to a network.

questions.question: What makes a system embedded?
questions.answer: It is built into a larger device for a specific task, often with limited resources.

questions.question: A thermostat measures temperature and switches heating on or off. Why is a thermostat controller an embedded system?
options: It is part of a heating system, with the specific task of controlling temperature.
Its Internet connection alone defines it as embedded.
It is a general-purpose computer because it accepts any desktop application.
Its screen size alone determines whether it is embedded.
questions.answer: A — It is part of a heating system, with the specific task of controlling temperature.

questions.question: “DNS assigns the same MAC address to all computers visiting a website.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Distributed DNS servers help look up the IP address associated with a domain name.
questions.explanation: Distributed DNS servers help look up the IP address associated with a domain name.

questions.question: RAM is full. Apps keep moving data between RAM and an SSD. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Virtual memory needs no secondary storage. (b) Virtual memory is faster than RAM because SSDs hold more.
questions.answer: (a) Virtual memory uses secondary storage when RAM is too full. (b) Moving data between RAM and slower secondary storage takes time. More storage space does not mean faster access.
questions.explanation: (a) Virtual memory uses secondary storage when RAM is too full. (b) Moving data between RAM and slower secondary storage takes time. More storage space does not mean faster access.

questions.question: What is a parameter?
questions.answer: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.
questions.explanation: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) Give a benefit of a high-level language. (2) Why might low-level code be chosen?
options: Runs directly without translation on every CPU / Equally portable across all architectures
Readable and usually more portable / Processor-specific control, harder to maintain
Runs directly without translation on every CPU / Processor-specific control, harder to maintain
Readable and usually more portable / Equally portable across all architectures
questions.answer: B — Readable and usually more portable / Processor-specific control, harder to maintain
questions.explanation: (1) It is usually more readable, maintainable and portable than processor-specific machine instructions. (2) It can provide close control of processor operations, but is harder to maintain and processor-dependent.

questions.question: “Adding active users always increases the bandwidth available to each user.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.
questions.explanation: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.

questions.question: A school needs central accounts and shared files. Three club laptops share files directly. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Every client must be a dedicated server. (b) Peer-to-peer needs a central server.
questions.answer: (a) A server manages shared services and resources for clients. (b) Peers share directly and can act as clients and servers. Central control suits a school; peer-to-peer can cost less for a small club but is harder to manage as it grows.
questions.explanation: (a) A server manages shared services and resources for clients. (b) Peers share directly and can act as clients and servers. Central control suits a school; peer-to-peer can cost less for a small club but is harder to manage as it grows.

questions.question: What does WHERE do in an SQL query?
questions.answer: It selects rows that meet a condition.
questions.explanation: It selects rows that meet a condition.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) What does a compiler normally do? (2) What does an interpreter normally do?
options: Translate before running; reusable executable / Always create standalone executable first
Retranslate each unchanged statement every run / Always create standalone executable first
Translate before running; reusable executable / Translate and execute during running
Retranslate each unchanged statement every run / Translate and execute during running
questions.answer: C — Translate before running; reusable executable / Translate and execute during running
questions.explanation: (1) It translates the program before execution, producing executable code that can be run again without retranslating unchanged source. (2) It translates and executes during running, usually statement by statement, aiding immediate testing feedback.

questions.question: “A router's main job is executing spreadsheet formulas.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It forwards traffic between different networks using IP addressing.
questions.explanation: It forwards traffic between different networks using IP addressing.

questions.question: A computer sends data to a printer on its LAN. “A switch sends every unicast frame to every port.” Correct this. How should the data reach the printer?
questions.answer: A switch uses MAC addresses to send data to the right connected device. It does not normally send each known unicast frame to every port.
questions.explanation: A switch uses MAC addresses to send data to the right connected device. It does not normally send each known unicast frame to every port.

questions.question: A £5-per-ticket program uses total = tickets + 5. What is the correction?
questions.answer: Use total = tickets * 5; addition does not calculate £5 for each ticket.
questions.explanation: Use total = tickets * 5; addition does not calculate £5 for each ticket.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) What is the IDE run-time environment for? (2) What does a translator integrated into an IDE provide?
options: Back up only; cannot execute / Compile or interpret for execution
Run/test and inspect output / Turn RAM into permanent storage
Back up only; cannot execute / Turn RAM into permanent storage
Run/test and inspect output / Compile or interpret for execution
questions.answer: D — Run/test and inspect output / Compile or interpret for execution

questions.question: “An IPv4 address is always six pairs of hexadecimal digits separated by colons.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: IPv4 supports addressing and routing. It is usually written as four decimal numbers separated by dots.

questions.question: An IDE finds a missing bracket. Once fixed, the program runs but gives the wrong total. Why did the IDE not prove the logic correct? What should you do next?

questions.question: What distinguishes a WAN?

questions.question: A school buys compatible networking equipment from different manufacturers. Why are computing standards useful?
options: Standards remove the need for agreed communication rules.
Agreed specifications help hardware and software from different producers interoperate.
All manufacturers must use incompatible proprietary interfaces.
Every computer must use the same brand of CPU to communicate.

questions.question: “SMTP's role is synchronising folders and read status across mail clients.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Sending email from a client to a mail server and between mail servers.
questions.explanation: Sending email from a client to a mail server and between mail servers.

questions.question: A star LAN has one central switch. “One broken workstation cable stops the whole network.” Correct this. Compare a broken cable with a failed switch.

questions.question: A network must continue operating if one connection fails. Why can a mesh topology be resilient?
options: A single central switch is the only possible communication path.
Extra links remove all installation and maintenance costs.
Other paths can keep data moving if some links fail. More links add cost and complexity.
Every possible journey has exactly one physical link with no alternatives.
questions.answer: C — Other paths can keep data moving if some links fail. More links add cost and complexity.
questions.explanation: Alternative paths can allow communication after some links fail, at the cost of more links and complexity.

questions.question: “Fibre carries electrical signals through copper wire.” Correct this. Explain why.

questions.question: “Bluetooth is normally the best choice for a high-capacity link between distant school sites.” Correct this. Explain why.

questions.question: An attacker automates repeated password guesses against an account. How does a brute-force attack work?
options: It tries many possible passwords or keys until one works.
It deceives a user through a trusted-looking message without trying passwords.
It only encrypts an existing user's own files for safekeeping.

questions.answer: A MAC address identifies a network interface on a LAN. It is usually six pairs of hexadecimal digits.

questions.question: Data must reach another network in the right order. “TCP chooses fonts; IP draws images.” Correct this. Explain each protocol's job.

questions.answer: Unsafe input changes an SQL query. An attacker may then view or change data.
questions.explanation: Unsafe input changes an SQL query. An attacker may then view or change data.

questions.question: A network administrator restricts incoming connections to approved services. How does a firewall protect a network?
options: It replaces the need for user accounts and permissions.
It uses rules to allow or block network traffic.
It encrypts every stored file automatically.
It guarantees that all online statements are true.

questions.explanation: It uses rules to allow or block network traffic.

questions.question: “HTTP is the protocol used only to send email to a mail server.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Transferring web resources between web clients and servers.

questions.question: A pupil logs in to a website. “HTTPS proves every website is honest.” Correct this. What does HTTPS protect?

options: Routine file compression to reduce network storage.
Automatic deletion of all users' data before security checks.
Testing with permission, within agreed limits, to find and fix security weaknesses.

questions.question: A new printer will not work. “A printer driver only stores website passwords.” Correct this. How could the right driver help?

questions.question: What is a typical feature of proprietary software?
questions.answer: Source code is normally controlled by its owner and users receive specified usage rights.
questions.explanation: Source code is normally controlled by its owner and users receive specified usage rights.

questions.question: A password used on another website has been leaked. Why are long unique passwords useful?

Sharing one administrator password with all users prevents misuse.
They make guessing harder and prevent reuse of a compromised password across accounts.

questions.question: “Defragmentation must speed up every SSD by moving its read head.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It brings file fragments together, reducing read-head movement when accessing a file.
questions.explanation: It brings file fragments together, reducing read-head movement when accessing a file.

questions.question: A program saves results and later reads attendance data. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Closing a file deletes it. (b) A program can read a file without opening it.
questions.answer: (a) Closing releases the file handle and helps finish buffered writes; it does not delete the file. (b) Opening creates a handle for access. Open, read or write, then close. Screen output does not save a file.

questions.question: Which law addresses unauthorised access to a computer system?
questions.answer: The Computer Misuse Act 1990.
questions.explanation: The Computer Misuse Act 1990.

questions.question: A school considers replacing functioning laptops every year. Give an environmental impact of frequent device replacement.
options: Manufacture and disposal have no material or energy costs.
Replacing a working device always eliminates all electronic waste.
Only the software version affects environmental impact.
Manufacturing uses energy and raw materials, and disposal can add electronic waste.
questions.answer: D — Manufacturing uses energy and raw materials, and disposal can add electronic waste.

questions.question: “Unauthorised access is lawful whenever the attacker does not delete files.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Unauthorised access to computer systems and related prohibited activities.
questions.explanation: Unauthorised access to computer systems and related prohibited activities.

questions.question: A pupil uses a browser and editor at once. Staff and pupils need different access rights. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Each app needs its own CPU. (b) Every user needs full access.

Everything legal is automatically ethical / What laws permit or prohibit

Everything legal is automatically ethical / Only what is popular

questions.lesson_title: Boolean Logic: AND, OR and NOT
questions.question: “Open source means there are never any licence conditions or costs.” Correct this. Explain why.

questions.lesson_title: Boolean Logic: AND, OR and NOT
questions.question: A computer needs maintenance and data protection. “Utilities are only apps for writing essays.” Correct this. What do utilities do?
questions.answer: Utilities maintain or protect a computer, adding tools beyond the OS. Writing an essay is an application task.
questions.explanation: Utilities maintain or protect a computer, adding tools beyond the OS. Writing an essay is an application task.

questions.question: How can you recognise a NOT gate symbol?
questions.answer: It is a one-input inverter, usually a triangle with a small output bubble.
questions.explanation: It is a one-input inverter, usually a triangle with a small output bubble.

questions.question: A teacher stores confidential records on a portable drive. What does an encryption utility do?
options: It assigns folder names without changing how readable data is stored.
It converts readable data into ciphertext using an algorithm and key to protect confidentiality.
It rearranges magnetic file fragments to reduce head movement.
It removes redundant information solely to reduce storage size.
questions.answer: B — It converts readable data into ciphertext using an algorithm and key to protect confidentiality.
questions.explanation: It converts readable data into ciphertext using an algorithm and key to protect confidentiality.

questions.question: “Publicly posting all personal records always improves privacy.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: People may lose control over how identifying information is used or shared.

questions.question: A login must get details, check them and choose the next step. “Algorithmic thinking means guessing steps in a random order.” Correct this. Why does order matter?

questions.question: How many input rows are needed for three independent Boolean inputs?

questions.question: A club copies paid software for all members without permission. What does copyright law protect in relation to software?
options: A program loses copyright protection whenever it is downloaded.
Only physical computer cases are protected; software never is.
Original software and other protected works, restricting unauthorised copying or distribution.
Owning one copy automatically permits unlimited redistribution.
questions.answer: C — Original software and other protected works, restricting unauthorised copying or distribution.
questions.explanation: Original software and other protected works, restricting unauthorised copying or distribution.

questions.question: 32 items are packed in boxes of 5. Use DIV and MOD to give the number of full boxes and leftover items.

questions.answer: An interpreter translates and runs code as it goes, often one statement at a time. This gives quick feedback during testing.

questions.question: A circuit has X = A AND B, followed by Q = X OR C. For A=1, B=0, C=1, which (X,Q) result is correct?

questions.question: “A count-controlled loop is only suitable when the number of repetitions can never be known.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: When the number of repetitions is known or determined by a fixed count.

questions.answer: A condition-controlled loop repeats until a condition tells it to stop. It need not run ten times. Choose the loop to suit the task and trace its steps.

questions.question: How do IDE error diagnostics help?
questions.answer: They show errors and often their location, helping the programmer find the cause.
questions.explanation: They show errors and often their location, helping the programmer find the cause.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) Which data type is suitable for a count of pupils? (2) Which type can represent a measured distance of 2.75 km?
options: Integer for a whole-number count / Fractional numeric value
Fractional value required for every count / Fractional numeric value
Integer for a whole-number count / Whole numbers only
Fractional value required for every count / Whole numbers only

A list of unrelated memory addresses with no shared entity.
A structure which must use the same data type for every named field.

grid[1,0] is 12; 12 is at grid[1,0].

teachingAdditions: Storage units and decimal conversions

A bit is one binary digit; a nibble is 4 bits and a byte is 8 bits. Using decimal units: 1 KB = 1,000 bytes; 1 MB = 1,000 KB; 1 GB = 1,000 MB; 1 TB = 1,000 GB; 1 PB = 1,000 TB. For example, 2 MB = 2,000 KB = 2,000,000 bytes; 2 TB = 2,000 GB.
Character capacity and adjacent codes

With n bits there are 2^n distinct binary patterns: 7 bits permit 128 codes. A character set must provide enough distinct codes for its characters. Unicode has several encodings; do not assume every character uses one byte. Given A=65 and consecutive capital-letter codes, B=66 and C=67. Derive supplied neighbouring codes rather than memorising ASCII values.

questions.answer: It brings file fragments together, reducing read-head movement when accessing a file.
questions.explanation: It brings file fragments together, reducing read-head movement when accessing a file.

questions.question: A password used on another website has been leaked. Why are long unique passwords useful?
options: Reusing one short password limits the effect of a website breach.
Using a public surname as every account password prevents guessing.
Sharing one administrator password with all users prevents misuse.
They make guessing harder and prevent reuse of a compromised password across accounts.
questions.answer: D — They make guessing harder and prevent reuse of a compromised password across accounts.
questions.explanation: They make guessing harder and prevent reuse of a compromised password across accounts.

questions.question: How does encryption protect transmitted data?
questions.answer: Encryption changes plaintext into ciphertext. Someone who intercepts it cannot easily read it without the key.
questions.explanation: Encryption changes plaintext into ciphertext. Someone who intercepts it cannot easily read it without the key.

questions.question: A 20 × 10 image at 8 bits per pixel has 200 bytes of raw pixel data, but its uncompressed file is larger. Explain why this need not be an error and name two metadata examples.
questions.answer: The file may include metadata or a header as well as pixels. Width, height and colour depth are examples. The formula counts only pixel data.
questions.explanation: The file may include metadata or a header as well as pixels. Width, height and colour depth are examples. The formula counts only pixel data.

questions.question: Give an environmental impact of frequent device replacement.
questions.answer: Manufacturing uses energy and raw materials, and disposal can add electronic waste.
questions.explanation: Manufacturing uses energy and raw materials, and disposal can add electronic waste.

questions.question: Visitors can otherwise enter a room containing network servers. Give a physical security measure and the threat it limits.
options: Lock the server room to limit access and reduce theft or tampering.
A strong password physically prevents somebody entering an unlocked room.
A compression utility prevents equipment from being stolen.
A software licence physically locks network cabinets.
questions.answer: A — Lock the server room to limit access and reduce theft or tampering.
questions.explanation: A locked server room restricts physical access and reduces opportunities for theft or tampering.

questions.question: A bitmap uses 3 bits per pixel. How many different colours are possible? If depth rises by one bit, what happens to the colour capacity?
questions.answer: 8 colours; one extra bit doubles capacity to 16.
questions.explanation: 8 colours; one extra bit doubles capacity to 16.
topics: Colour-depth quality size and colour count

questions.question: An image is 30 × 20 pixels. Both dimensions double at the same colour depth. What happens to pixel count and raw size? Explain.
questions.answer: (a) 600 pixels become 2,400. Raw size is four times larger because both dimensions double.
questions.explanation: (a) 600 pixels become 2,400. Raw size is four times larger because both dimensions double.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Data Protection Act 2018?
questions.answer: It sets rules for using personal data lawfully and protects people's rights.
questions.explanation: It sets rules for using personal data lawfully and protects people's rights.

questions.question: A device stores 72 bits. How many bytes and how many nibbles is that?
options: 72 bytes and 72 nibbles.
9 bytes and 18 nibbles.
18 bytes and 9 nibbles.
576 bytes and 288 nibbles.
questions.answer: B — 9 bytes and 18 nibbles.
questions.explanation: 9 bytes and 18 nibbles.

questions.question: A text file contains 180 characters. The stated encoding uses 8 bits per character. Calculate its raw size in bits and bytes.
questions.answer: 1,440 bits and 180 bytes.
questions.explanation: 1,440 bits and 180 bytes.

questions.question: A microphone records digital sound. “Sampling stores every instant of the sound wave.” Correct this. How does it affect recorded detail?
questions.answer: Measure amplitude at regular intervals. Store each rounded (quantised) value in binary. Sample rate and bit depth limit the detail captured.
questions.explanation: Measure amplitude at regular intervals. Store each rounded (quantised) value in binary. Sample rate and bit depth limit the detail captured.

questions.question: What does the Computer Misuse Act 1990 address?
questions.answer: Unauthorised access to computer systems and related prohibited activities.
questions.explanation: Unauthorised access to computer systems and related prohibited activities.

questions.question: A small image contains differently coloured pixels. How does a bitmap represent pixel colours?
options: By storing each pixel as a continuous analogue voltage in the file.
By storing only the image's filename, with no colour information.
Each pixel has a colour code stored in binary.
By recording only one overall colour for the entire image.
questions.answer: C — Each pixel has a colour code stored in binary.
questions.explanation: Each pixel has a colour code stored in binary.

questions.question: “RAM keeps every saved file permanently after shutdown.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: The program's active instructions and working data.
questions.explanation: The program's active instructions and working data.

questions.question: A mono recorder stores sound samples. Two recordings have the same sample rate and length but different bit depths. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Sample rate is bits per sample. (b) Bit depth is samples per second.
questions.answer: (a) Sample rate means samples per second: 8,000 Hz means 8,000 samples each second. A higher rate can add detail and use more space. (b) Bit depth is bits per sample; more bits allow more amplitude levels and use more space. Longer duration adds samples.
questions.explanation: (a) Sample rate means samples per second: 8,000 Hz means 8,000 samples each second. A higher rate can add detail and use more space. (b) Bit depth is bits per sample; more bits allow more amplitude levels and use more space. Longer duration adds samples.

questions.question: What is a key feature of an open-source licence?
questions.answer: It permits access to source code and modification or redistribution under its conditions.
questions.explanation: It permits access to source code and modification or redistribution under its conditions.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) How does the OS support memory management and multitasking? (2) What does OS user management include?
options: One permanently dedicated CPU per application / Manage accounts and access rights
Allocate memory and manage processor time / Identical unrestricted rights for all
One permanently dedicated CPU per application / Identical unrestricted rights for all
Allocate memory and manage processor time / Manage accounts and access rights
questions.answer: D — Allocate memory and manage processor time / Manage accounts and access rights
questions.explanation: (1) It allocates memory and manages resources and processor time among running applications. (2) Managing accounts, authentication and access rights.

questions.question: “A longer recording automatically has finer amplitude accuracy.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It doubles size but does not by itself improve sampling quality.
questions.explanation: It doubles size but does not by itself improve sampling quality.
topics: Duration effect on size versus quality

questions.question: A mono clip uses 1,000 samples/s for 3 s at 8 bits/sample. Calculate its raw size in bytes, excluding headers and compression.
questions.answer: (a) 1,000 × 3 × 8 = 24,000 bits; divide by 8 = 3,000 bytes.
questions.explanation: (a) 1,000 × 3 × 8 = 24,000 bits; divide by 8 = 3,000 bytes.

questions.question: What makes a technology issue ethical?
questions.answer: It concerns fairness, responsibility or what ought to be done, even if an action is legal.
questions.explanation: It concerns fairness, responsibility or what ought to be done, even if an action is legal.

questions.question: A pupil carries files between computers on a USB flash drive. Which technology does a USB flash drive use?
options: Solid-state storage with no moving read/write mechanism.
Optical technology read using a laser.
Magnetic technology with spinning platters.
Volatile working memory that loses all stored files when unplugged.
questions.answer: A — Solid-state storage with no moving read/write mechanism.
questions.explanation: Solid-state storage with no moving read/write mechanism.

questions.question: “Compression must increase every file's size.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Reducing file size can reduce storage requirements and transmission time.
questions.explanation: Reducing file size can reduce storage requirements and transmission time.

questions.question: A website thumbnail may tolerate a small reduction in detail. “Lossy compression guarantees an identical original after decompression.” Correct this. What could happen?
questions.answer: Lossy compression removes information, so the exact original may be lost. A thumbnail can lose some detail; source code must be restored exactly.
questions.explanation: Lossy compression removes information, so the exact original may be lost. A thumbnail can lose some detail; source code must be restored exactly.

questions.question: What is decomposition?
questions.answer: Breaking a complex problem into smaller manageable subproblems.
questions.explanation: Breaking a complex problem into smaller manageable subproblems.

questions.question: A pupil needs to rename a file and move it into a revision folder. What does operating-system file management do?
options: Convert character codes from one language into another.
It manages files and folders: naming, saving, copying, moving and deleting them.
Execute arithmetic and logical CPU instructions.
Choose the next instruction address during the fetch cycle.
questions.answer: B — It manages files and folders: naming, saving, copying, moving and deleting them.
questions.explanation: It organises and manages files and folders, including naming, saving, copying, moving and deleting.

questions.question: “Lossless compression deliberately removes arbitrary source-code characters.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Lossless compression restores the original exactly. Losing source-code characters could break the program.
questions.explanation: Lossless compression restores the original exactly. Losing source-code characters could break the program.

questions.question: A computer needs maintenance and data protection. “Utilities are only apps for writing essays.” Correct this. What do utilities do?
questions.answer: Utilities maintain or protect a computer, adding tools beyond the OS. Writing an essay is an application task.
questions.explanation: Utilities maintain or protect a computer, adding tools beyond the OS. Writing an essay is an application task.

questions.question: What is algorithmic thinking?
questions.answer: Developing a clear, ordered and unambiguous method for solving a problem.
questions.explanation: Developing a clear, ordered and unambiguous method for solving a problem.

questions.question: A teacher stores confidential records on a portable drive. What does an encryption utility do?
options: It removes redundant information solely to reduce storage size.
It assigns folder names without changing how readable data is stored.
It converts readable data into ciphertext using an algorithm and key to protect confidentiality.
It rearranges magnetic file fragments to reduce head movement.
questions.answer: C — It converts readable data into ciphertext using an algorithm and key to protect confidentiality.
questions.explanation: It converts readable data into ciphertext using an algorithm and key to protect confidentiality.

questions.question: What does a compression utility do?
questions.answer: It reduces the storage space required for data, using a suitable lossless or lossy method.
questions.explanation: It reduces the storage space required for data, using a suitable lossless or lossy method.

questions.question: A CPU reads an instruction at memory address 120. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) MAR holds a calculation result. (b) MDR always holds the next instruction's address.
questions.answer: (a) The MAR holds the address being accessed. (b) The MDR holds data or an instruction moving to or from memory. An address is different from the data at it.
questions.explanation: (a) The MAR holds the address being accessed. (b) The MDR holds data or an instruction moving to or from memory. An address is different from the data at it.

questions.question: For cost = price × quantity, identify input, processing and output.
questions.answer: Inputs: price and quantity. Processing: multiplication. Output: total cost.
questions.explanation: Inputs: price and quantity. Processing: multiplication. Output: total cost.

questions.question: A business wants to copy and distribute licensed software. What makes a technology issue legal?
options: Only whether most users find an action convenient.
Only whether a technical operation is fast.
Only whether the action is fashionable or popular.
It concerns what relevant laws permit or prohibit.
questions.answer: D — It concerns what relevant laws permit or prohibit.
questions.explanation: It concerns what relevant laws permit or prohibit.

questions.question: What is a privacy concern with collecting personal data?
questions.answer: People may lose control over how identifying information is used or shared.
questions.explanation: People may lose control over how identifying information is used or shared.

questions.question: An online service uses only one language. “Technology cannot affect language or who takes part.” Correct this. Who might be left out?
questions.answer: Technology can change language, access, traditions and who can take part. Consider who benefits or is harmed. Something legal may still be unfair.
questions.explanation: Technology can change language, access, traditions and who can take part. Consider who benefits or is harmed. Something legal may still be unfair.
