questions.question: What does a diamond represent in a flowchart?
questions.answer: A decision or condition with alternative paths.
questions.explanation: A decision or condition with alternative paths.

questions.question: A spreadsheet is open and its cells are being recalculated. Why is primary storage needed?
options: It holds instructions and working data that the CPU needs while programs run.
Only to hold backups that are never accessed during execution.
Only to retain user files indefinitely after power loss.
To replace the CPU's ability to execute instructions.
questions.answer: A — It holds instructions and working data that the CPU needs while programs run.
questions.explanation: It holds instructions and working data that the CPU needs while programs run.

questions.question: “Both RAM and ROM lose their contents when power is removed.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: RAM loses its contents; ROM keeps its contents because it is non-volatile.
questions.explanation: RAM loses its contents; ROM keeps its contents because it is non-volatile.

questions.question: A computer needs startup instructions when switched on. “ROM normally holds all unsaved user work while applications run.” Correct this. What could happen?
questions.answer: ROM keeps firmware or startup instructions without power. These let the computer start when switched on.
questions.explanation: ROM keeps firmware or startup instructions without power. These let the computer start when switched on.

questions.question: Why must a trace table follow executed assignments in order?
questions.answer: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.
questions.explanation: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.

questions.question: A repeated operation needs the same data many times. Where is CPU cache and why is it useful?
options: In a backup folder, used only when the computer is off.
Cache is in or near the CPU. It gives faster access to often-used data and instructions than main memory.
On a remote server, replacing every memory transfer with Internet access.
In an optical disc drive, keeping all working values after shutdown.
questions.answer: B — Cache is in or near the CPU. It gives faster access to often-used data and instructions than main memory.
questions.explanation: It is in or close to the CPU and supplies frequently used instructions or data faster than main memory.

questions.question: “Secondary storage is needed because RAM permanently keeps every file.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It keeps programs and files when power is off and usually provides lots of storage space.
questions.explanation: It keeps programs and files when power is off and usually provides lots of storage space.

questions.question: A school uses DVDs for read-only videos and an HDD for a large archive. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) DVDs are magnetic. (b) HDDs use only flash chips and have no moving parts.
questions.answer: (a) A DVD uses optical storage, read by a laser. (b) An HDD uses magnetic storage on spinning platters. Moving parts and portability affect which is suitable.
questions.explanation: (a) A DVD uses optical storage, read by a laser. (b) An HDD uses magnetic storage on spinning platters. Moving parts and portability affect which is suitable.

questions.question: Name one operating-system function.
questions.answer: Memory management, user management, file management, a user interface or peripheral management.
questions.explanation: Memory management, user management, file management, a user interface or peripheral management.

questions.question: A club copies paid software for all members without permission. What does copyright law protect in relation to software?
options: A program loses copyright protection whenever it is downloaded.
Only physical computer cases are protected; software never is.
Original software and other protected works, restricting unauthorised copying or distribution.
Owning one copy automatically permits unlimited redistribution.
questions.answer: C — Original software and other protected works, restricting unauthorised copying or distribution.
questions.explanation: Original software and other protected works, restricting unauthorised copying or distribution.

questions.question: What is a typical feature of proprietary software?
questions.answer: Source code is normally controlled by its owner and users receive specified usage rights.
questions.explanation: Source code is normally controlled by its owner and users receive specified usage rights.

questions.question: A school needs a large, cheap archive drive. A pupil's only coursework copy is on an SSD. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) An HDD is always faster and tougher than an SSD. (b) An SSD never fails, so needs no backup.
questions.answer: (a) An HDD can give lots of space at low cost per GB. Check the device and task. (b) An SSD can fail through faults or wear, so keep backups. No device is best at everything.
questions.explanation: (a) An HDD can give lots of space at low cost per GB. Check the device and task. (b) An SSD can fail through faults or wear, so keep backups. No device is best at everything.

questions.question: What is the difference between input and output?
questions.answer: Input enters a program; output is information the program produces.
questions.explanation: Input enters a program; output is information the program produces.

questions.question: An application loads many small files from scattered locations. Why is an SSD often faster than an HDD for random access?
options: Its magnetic read head spins faster than the HDD's head.
It stores all data only in volatile RAM.
Its larger capacity alone guarantees a lower access time.
It does not need a moving head to seek positions on spinning platters.
questions.answer: D — It does not need a moving head to seek positions on spinning platters.
questions.explanation: It does not need a moving head to seek positions on spinning platters.

questions.question: “Portability and durability mean exactly the same thing.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: No moving read/write parts makes an SSD less likely to be damaged by shocks. Size and weight also affect portability.
questions.explanation: No moving read/write parts makes an SSD less likely to be damaged by shocks. Size and weight also affect portability.

questions.question: A journey planner needs stops and times, but not bus-seat colours. “Abstraction removes every detail, even inputs.” Correct this. What should the planner keep?
questions.answer: Remove details that are not needed. Keep the information and parts needed to solve the problem, then link clear steps.
questions.explanation: Remove details that are not needed. Keep the information and parts needed to solve the problem, then link clear steps.

teachingAdditions: Constants and suitable types

A constant is a named value intended to remain unchanged during execution, such as MAX_CLASS_SIZE=30. A variable such as score changes. Integer stores whole numbers; real can store fractional values such as 2.75. A character is one character such as a middle initial; a string is a sequence such as a full name.

questions.question: What does assignment do to a variable?
questions.answer: It stores a value in the named variable, replacing its previous value if one existed.
questions.explanation: It stores a value in the named variable, replacing its previous value if one existed.

questions.question: A laptop runs a program that adds two scores. What is the CPU's main purpose?
options: It executes instructions to process data.
Retain all programs permanently without power.
Forward packets between remote networks.
Provide the physical pixels of the display.
questions.answer: A — It executes instructions to process data.
questions.explanation: It executes instructions to process data.

questions.question: A folder contains 30 images of 200 KB each. Using decimal units, give its total size in KB and MB.
prerequisite_notes: Add a worked multiple-file capacity example before retrieval.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: A photographer travels with large files and needs fast transfers. “The cheapest storage is always best.” Correct this. What else matters?
questions.answer: Check capacity, speed, cost and how it will be used. An SSD can suit fast transfers and travel, if its capacity and price meet the photographer's needs.
questions.explanation: Check capacity, speed, cost and how it will be used. An SSD can suit fast transfers and travel, if its capacity and price meet the photographer's needs.

teachingAdditions: Integer arithmetic and exponentiation

In OCR ERL, 17 DIV 5 is the integer quotient 3, while 17 MOD 5 is the remainder 2. The ^ operator means exponentiation: 2 ^ 3 = 8. Ordinary precedence applies; 4 + 3 * 2 = 10, whereas (4 + 3) * 2 = 14.

questions.question: What are 17 DIV 5 and 17 MOD 5?
questions.answer: DIV gives integer quotient 3; MOD gives remainder 2.
questions.explanation: DIV gives integer quotient 3; MOD gives remainder 2.
prerequisite_notes: Explicitly teach integer quotient and remainder with examples; do not infer coverage from ordinary division.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) What happens during the fetch stage? (2) What happens during the decode stage?
options: Carry out its calculation / Save all source code permanently
Obtain next instruction from memory / Interpret the fetched instruction
Carry out its calculation / Interpret the fetched instruction
Obtain next instruction from memory / Save all source code permanently
questions.answer: B — Obtain next instruction from memory / Interpret the fetched instruction
questions.explanation: (1) The next instruction is obtained from memory. (2) The instruction is interpreted so the required operation can be identified.

questions.question: “Execution only copies an instruction into memory without performing it.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: The operation specified by the decoded instruction is carried out.
questions.explanation: The operation specified by the decoded instruction is carried out.

questions.question: A CPU compares scores and adds a bonus. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) The Control Unit stores documents forever. (b) The ALU stores the next instruction's address.
questions.answer: (a) The Control Unit decodes instructions and controls CPU operations. (b) The ALU handles arithmetic and logic. Registers store data or addresses briefly.
questions.explanation: (a) The Control Unit decodes instructions and controls CPU operations. (b) The ALU handles arithmetic and logic. Registers store data or addresses briefly.

teachingAdditions: Boolean is a data type

A Boolean stores true or false. For example, complete=false is a Boolean state; it is different from the string "false". Comparisons such as score>=50 produce Boolean results that can be combined using AND, OR and NOT.

questions.question: When is A AND B true?
questions.answer: Only when both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Only when both A and B are true.

questions.question: A loop repeatedly uses the same instructions. What does CPU cache hold?
options: Every user's complete archive after shutdown.
Only values arriving through a network cable.
Frequently or recently used data and instructions for rapid access.
Only the address of the next instruction.
questions.answer: C — Frequently or recently used data and instructions for rapid access.
questions.explanation: Frequently or recently used data and instructions for rapid access.

questions.question: “A register is a large external drive used for backups.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A small, fast storage location inside the CPU. It holds data or addresses in use.
questions.explanation: A small, fast storage location inside the CPU. It holds data or addresses in use.
topics: Registers as small fast CPU storage

questions.question: The next instruction is at address 240. An addition gives 18. What do the accumulator and Program Counter hold? Explain the difference.
questions.answer: The accumulator holds the result, 18. The PC holds the next instruction's address, 240.
questions.explanation: The accumulator holds the result, 18. The PC holds the next instruction's address, 240.

questions.question: What does selection do?
questions.answer: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.
questions.explanation: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.

questions.question: A quiz is split into menu, play and results; play is split into input and scoring. What does a structure diagram show?
options: The runtime order of decisions and loops only.
The physical connections between network switches only.
The sequence of memory addresses fetched by the CPU only.
A problem's main sections, their subdivisions and the links or hierarchy between them.
questions.answer: D — A problem's main sections, their subdivisions and the links or hierarchy between them.
questions.explanation: A problem's main sections, their subdivisions and the links or hierarchy between them.

questions.question: “Doubling clock speed guarantees every program finishes in exactly half the time.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: More clock cycles per second. This may let the CPU process more instructions if other factors are similar.
questions.explanation: More clock cycles per second. This may let the CPU process more instructions if other factors are similar.

questions.question: A user runs several apps. Some work can be shared across cores. “Each extra core doubles every program's speed.” Correct this. When do more cores help?
questions.answer: More cores help when work can be split between them. Other CPU features and the task also affect the speed gained.
questions.explanation: More cores help when work can be split between them. Other CPU features and the task also affect the speed gained.

questions.question: What does selection do?
questions.answer: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.
questions.explanation: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.

questions.question: A program's next instruction is at address 240. What does the Program Counter hold?
options: The address of the next instruction to be fetched.
The value of the last arithmetic result.
The contents of every RAM location.
A count of all installed programs.
questions.answer: A — The address of the next instruction to be fetched.
questions.explanation: The address of the next instruction to be fetched.

questions.question: “Larger cache increases the number of installed CPU cores.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A larger cache holds more often-used data and instructions. This can reduce slower memory access.
questions.explanation: A larger cache holds more often-used data and instructions. This can reduce slower memory access.

questions.question: CPU A: 4 GHz, two cores, 2 MB cache. CPU B: 3 GHz, eight cores, 8 MB cache. Why is neither fastest for every task?
questions.answer: A has more cycles per second, which may help one task. B has more cores for parallel work and more cache to reduce slow memory access. Speed also depends on the task and CPU design.
questions.explanation: A has more cycles per second, which may help one task. B has more cores for parallel work and more cache to reduce slow memory access. Speed also depends on the task and CPU design.

questions.question: When is a count-controlled loop suitable?
questions.answer: When the number of repetitions is known or determined by a fixed count.
questions.explanation: When the number of repetitions is known or determined by a fixed count.

questions.question: A programmer plans an age-checking algorithm before coding it. Why use pseudocode when designing an algorithm?
options: It guarantees an incorrect algorithm becomes correct without testing.
Pseudocode shows steps in order without needing one programming language's exact syntax.
It must use valid binary machine instructions for one processor.
It can only describe how the interface looks, never processing.
questions.answer: B — Pseudocode shows steps in order without needing one programming language's exact syntax.
questions.explanation: It expresses ordered algorithmic steps without requiring the exact syntax of one programming language.

questions.question: “A diamond is used only for unconditional calculations.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A decision or condition with alternative paths.
questions.explanation: A decision or condition with alternative paths.

questions.question: A program works out a bill, then applies a discount. “The order of steps never matters.” Correct this. What could go wrong?
questions.answer: Steps must be clear and in the right order. Check that conditions give the right result for every allowed input.
questions.explanation: Steps must be clear and in the right order. Check that conditions give the right result for every allowed input.

questions.question: When is a condition-controlled loop suitable?
questions.answer: When repetition continues or ends according to a condition, such as valid input.
questions.explanation: When repetition continues or ends according to a condition, such as valid input.

questions.question: Linear-search [7, 2, 9, 4] for 4, starting at index 0. List the values checked. How many comparisons are needed?
options: Only inspect the first item, whatever the target.
Skip every item at an odd index.
[7, 2, 9, 4]; 4 comparison(s), found at index 3.
Stop without comparisons because linear search needs sorted data.
questions.answer: C — [7, 2, 9, 4]; 4 comparison(s), found at index 3.
questions.explanation: [7, 2, 9, 4]; 4 comparison(s), found at index 3.

questions.question: “An IF statement must execute every possible branch regardless of its condition.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.
questions.explanation: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.

questions.question: Do one bubble-sort pass from left to right, smallest to largest, on [6, 1, 5, 3]. Show the array after each comparison. Which value ends up on the right?
questions.answer: (a) [[1, 6, 5, 3], [1, 5, 6, 3], [1, 5, 3, 6]]; largest value 6 is at the right end.
questions.explanation: (a) [[1, 6, 5, 3], [1, 5, 6, 3], [1, 5, 3, 6]]; largest value 6 is at the right end.

questions.question: Why must a trace table follow executed assignments in order?
questions.answer: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.
questions.explanation: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) Which data type is suitable for a count of pupils? (2) Which type can represent a measured distance of 2.75 km?

Integer for a whole-number count / Whole numbers only

Integer for a whole-number count / Fractional numeric value

questions.question: How do character and string data differ?
questions.answer: A character represents one character; a string represents a sequence of characters.

prerequisite_notes: Explicitly distinguish a single character from a string.

questions.question: What does sequence mean in programming?
questions.answer: Instructions execute in the specified order.
questions.explanation: Instructions execute in the specified order.

questions.question: A bill calculator multiplies a quantity by a unit price before adding a fee. What is 4 + 3 * 2 with ordinary operator precedence?
options: 10, because multiplication is evaluated before addition.
14, because addition is evaluated before multiplication.
20, because all values must be multiplied.
11, because 3 * 2 is treated as 7.
questions.answer: A — 10, because multiplication is evaluated before addition.
questions.explanation: 10, because multiplication is evaluated before addition.

questions.answer: 8; ^ denotes exponentiation in OCR ERL.

questions.question: Join text '12' to '3'. Then convert '12' to an integer and add 3. Give both results. What should happen if the input is 'twelve'?
questions.answer: Joining the strings gives '123'. Converting '12' to an integer and adding 3 gives 15. Handle or reject 'twelve': it cannot be cast to an integer directly.
questions.explanation: Joining the strings gives '123'. Converting '12' to an integer and adding 3 gives 15. Handle or reject 'twelve': it cannot be cast to an integer directly.

questions.question: A £5-per-ticket program uses total = tickets + 5. What is the correction?
questions.answer: Use total = tickets * 5; addition does not calculate £5 for each ticket.
questions.explanation: Use total = tickets * 5; addition does not calculate £5 for each ticket.

questions.question: Insertion sort has sorted part [2, 5, 8] and next value 6. Which values move? Give the new sorted part.
options: New prefix [2, 5, 8]; discard the key.
Values greater than 6 shift right: [8]. New prefix [2, 5, 6, 8].
New prefix [2, 5, 8, 6]; no comparison is needed.
New prefix [6, 2, 5, 8]; always place the key first.
questions.answer: B — Values greater than 6 shift right: [8]. New prefix [2, 5, 6, 8].

questions.question: “A comparison operator must always produce a text paragraph.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A Boolean result: true or false.
questions.explanation: A Boolean result: true or false.

questions.question: A warning needs high temperature OR high pressure. “OR is false when both inputs are true.” Correct this. What happens when both are high?
questions.answer: OR is true if at least one input is true, including both. AND needs both true. NOT reverses a value.
questions.explanation: OR is true if at least one input is true, including both. AND needs both true. NOT reverses a value.

questions.question: What does assignment do to a variable?
questions.answer: It stores a value in the named variable, replacing its previous value if one existed.
questions.explanation: It stores a value in the named variable, replacing its previous value if one existed.

questions.question: A program must continue only while finished is false. What does NOT do to a Boolean value?
options: It always returns true for both possible inputs.
It always returns false for both possible inputs.
It reverses true and false.
It copies its Boolean input without changing it.
questions.answer: C — It reverses true and false.
questions.explanation: It reverses true and false.

questions.question: What values does a Boolean variable represent?
questions.answer: True or false.
questions.explanation: True or false.

questions.question: Computers share files on one school site. Two sites in different towns also need a link. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) A LAN spans several countries. (b) A WAN only works in one room.
questions.answer: (a) A LAN covers a small area, such as a school site. (b) A WAN links networks over a large area, often using outside providers' links. Internet access alone does not decide the type.
questions.explanation: (a) A LAN covers a small area, such as a school site. (b) A WAN links networks over a large area, often using outside providers' links. Internet access alone does not decide the type.

questions.question: What is the result of concatenating 'AB' and '12'?
questions.answer: AB12, with no automatically inserted space.
questions.explanation: AB12, with no automatically inserted space.

questions.question: A four-element array stores [4, 8, 2, 6]. What is a one-dimensional array?
options: A structure whose first OCR ERL index is always one.
A collection in which every element must have a different name rather than an index.
A structure that automatically gains a new element after every indexed read.
A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.
questions.answer: D — A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.
questions.explanation: A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.

questions.question: “Testing a few inputs proves a program can never contain any fault.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: To identify faults and check behaviour against requirements using expected results.
questions.explanation: To identify faults and check behaviour against requirements using expected results.

questions.question: A programmer tests input code while building a booking program, then tests the finished program. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Iterative testing starts only after delivery. (b) Final testing removes the need for earlier tests.
questions.answer: (a) Iterative testing checks and fixes parts while building the program. (b) Final testing checks the finished program against its requirements. Both are needed.
questions.explanation: (a) Iterative testing checks and fixes parts while building the program. (b) Final testing checks the finished program against its requirements. Both are needed.

questions.question: What does input validation check?
questions.answer: Whether input meets specified rules; it does not prove factual truth or identity.
questions.explanation: Whether input meets specified rules; it does not prove factual truth or identity.
topics: Validation rules and rejection of invalid data

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) For valid integer ages 13–18, give an invalid input of the correct type. (2) For a numeric age input, give erroneous data of the wrong type.
options: Correct type outside rules, e.g. 12 / Wrong type, e.g. text 'twelve'
Always wrong data type / Wrong type, e.g. text 'twelve'
Correct type outside rules, e.g. 12 / Always a valid in-range integer
Always wrong data type / Always a valid in-range integer
questions.answer: A — Correct type outside rules, e.g. 12 / Wrong type, e.g. text 'twelve'
questions.explanation: (1) 12 is an integer but outside the valid range, so it must be rejected. (2) The text 'twelve' is the wrong data type and must be handled or rejected.

questions.question: “Defensive design assumes every user always enters valid and harmless data.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Planning for invalid, unexpected or malicious use and handling it safely.
questions.explanation: Planning for invalid, unexpected or malicious use and handling it safely.

questions.question: A desktop needs a LAN connection. “A NIC keeps files when power is off.” Correct this. What does a NIC do here?
questions.answer: A NIC lets a device connect to a network. It has a different job from storage or a router.
questions.explanation: A NIC lets a device connect to a network. It has a different job from storage or a router.

questions.question: What is a one-dimensional array?
questions.answer: A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.
questions.explanation: A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) For valid ages 13–18, give an ordinary normal test value. (2) For valid ages 13–18, identify the two valid boundary values.
options: Wrong type required / Valid edge values 12 and 19
Ordinary valid input, e.g. 15 / Valid edge values 13 and 18
Wrong type required / Valid edge values 13 and 18
Ordinary valid input, e.g. 15 / Valid edge values 12 and 19
questions.answer: B — Ordinary valid input, e.g. 15 / Valid edge values 13 and 18
questions.explanation: (1) 15 is a representative valid value away from the boundaries. (2) 13 and 18 lie on the edges of the valid range.

questions.question: “Any device connected to the Internet is automatically an embedded system.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It is part of a heating system, with the specific task of controlling temperature.
questions.explanation: It is part of a heating system, with the specific task of controlling temperature.

questions.question: A pupil enters a domain name. “DNS gives the same MAC address to every visitor.” Correct this. How does DNS help find the website?
questions.answer: DNS servers look up the IP address for a domain name. Access needs the relevant server and network services to work.
questions.explanation: DNS servers look up the IP address for a domain name. Access needs the relevant server and network services to work.

questions.question: How can a loop total an array's values?
questions.answer: Set a total to 0. Loop through the array, adding each value once.
questions.explanation: Set a total to 0. Loop through the array, adding each value once.

questions.question: A washing machine's controller monitors sensors and controls its wash cycle. What makes a system embedded?
options: It must always have Internet access and a keyboard.
It is defined only by having more RAM than a desktop.
It is built into a larger device for a specific task, often with limited resources.
It must run arbitrary desktop applications for many unrelated tasks.
questions.answer: C — It is built into a larger device for a specific task, often with limited resources.
questions.explanation: It is built into a larger device to perform a dedicated function, often with limited resources.

questions.question: “Adding active users always increases the bandwidth available to each user.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.
questions.explanation: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.

questions.question: A school needs central accounts and shared files. Three club laptops share files directly. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Every client must be a dedicated server. (b) Peer-to-peer needs a central server.
questions.answer: (a) A server manages shared services and resources for clients. (b) Peers share directly and can act as clients and servers. Central control suits a school; peer-to-peer can cost less for a small club but is harder to manage as it grows.
questions.explanation: (a) A server manages shared services and resources for clients. (b) Peers share directly and can act as clients and servers. Central control suits a school; peer-to-peer can cost less for a small club but is harder to manage as it grows.

questions.question: How is a cell selected in a two-dimensional array?
questions.answer: Use two indexes: one for the row and one for the column.
questions.explanation: Use two indexes: one for the row and one for the column.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) What is a router's main network role? (2) What does a switch do within a LAN?
options: Calculates spreadsheet formulas / Forwards within LAN using MAC
Routes between networks using IP / Broadcasts every unicast frame to all ports
Calculates spreadsheet formulas / Broadcasts every unicast frame to all ports
Routes between networks using IP / Forwards within LAN using MAC
questions.answer: D — Routes between networks using IP / Forwards within LAN using MAC
questions.explanation: (1) It forwards traffic between different networks using IP addressing. (2) It forwards data towards the appropriate connected device using MAC-address information.

questions.question: “An IPv4 address is always six pairs of hexadecimal digits separated by colons.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: IPv4 supports addressing and routing. It is usually written as four decimal numbers separated by dots.
questions.explanation: IPv4 supports addressing and routing. It is usually written as four decimal numbers separated by dots.

questions.question: Tablets need to join a wired LAN. “A WAP changes domain names into IP addresses.” Correct this. How does a WAP help the tablets?
questions.answer: A wireless access point connects wireless devices to a network. It has a different job from a switch or router.
questions.explanation: A wireless access point connects wireless devices to a network. It has a different job from a switch or router.

questions.question: What is a record?
questions.answer: Named fields about one item or person. Fields may have different data types.
questions.explanation: Named fields about one item or person. Fields may have different data types.

questions.question: A programmer changes an upper-bound comparison from < to <=. Why retest after refining an algorithm?
options: To check that the fault is fixed and that other required behaviour still works.
A corrected line guarantees every requirement now works without checking.
Only delete the old test inputs and assume success.
Test no boundary values because the boundary comparison was edited.
questions.answer: A — To check that the fault is fixed and that other required behaviour still works.
questions.explanation: To check that the fault is fixed and that other required behaviour still works.

questions.question: “The Internet is a single computer containing every website.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A worldwide collection of interconnected computer networks.
questions.explanation: A worldwide collection of interconnected computer networks.

questions.question: A browser asks for a school's web page. “A client must host a website before asking for it.” Correct this. Which computer provides the page?
questions.answer: A web server stores website resources and sends them when clients request them. Access needs working servers and network services.
questions.explanation: A web server stores website resources and sends them when clients request them. Access needs working servers and network services.

questions.question: What distinguishes a function from a procedure?
questions.answer: A function returns a value to the caller. A procedure performs a task without returning a function value.
questions.explanation: A function returns a value to the caller. A procedure performs a task without returning a function value.

questions.question: A user presses Send on a new email. What is SMTP used for?
options: Transferring ordinary web pages from a web server to a browser.
Sending email from a client to a mail server and between mail servers.
Synchronising read status across multiple mail clients.
Downloading stored incoming email for local retrieval.
questions.answer: B — Sending email from a client to a mail server and between mail servers.
questions.explanation: Sending email from a client to a mail server and between mail servers.

questions.question: “Cloud storage guarantees that files remain accessible during every Internet outage.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Storage, software or processing on remote servers, accessed over a network. Access depends on the connection and service.
questions.explanation: Storage, software or processing on remote servers, accessed over a network. Access depends on the connection and service.

questions.question: A school buys network devices from different makers. “Standards mean all devices must have the same maker.” Correct this. How do standards help?
questions.answer: Agreed standards let hardware and software from different makers work together and exchange data.
questions.explanation: Agreed standards let hardware and software from different makers work together and exchange data.

teachingAdditions: Local and global constants as well as variables

A local variable or constant is accessible within its defining local scope. A global variable or constant has wider program scope. Constants are intended to stay fixed during execution; variables may change. Unnecessary mutable global state makes unintended changes harder to track.

questions.question: When might a procedure be suitable?
questions.answer: For a named reusable task such as displaying a menu when no function result is required.
questions.explanation: For a named reusable task such as displaying a menu when no function result is required.

questions.question: In OCR ERL, s = 'VARIABLE'. Give s.substring(1,3), then explain what each argument means.
options: AR; second argument is an exclusive end index.
IAB; start at index 3.
ARI; start at zero-based index 1 and take 3 characters.
VAR; indexing starts at 1.
questions.answer: C — ARI; start at zero-based index 1 and take 3 characters.
questions.explanation: ARI; start at zero-based index 1 and take 3 characters.

questions.question: “Failure of any one workstation cable necessarily disables all other star-network links.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: If the central switch fails, devices using it lose contact. A broken cable usually affects just one workstation.
questions.explanation: If the central switch fails, devices using it lose contact. A broken cable usually affects just one workstation.

questions.question: A network must cope if one link fails. “A mesh has only one path between any two devices.” Correct this. How could it keep working?
questions.answer: A mesh has other paths if some links fail. More links add cost and complexity. Check the paths that remain.
questions.explanation: A mesh has other paths if some links fail. More links add cost and complexity. Check the paths that remain.

teachingAdditions: Passing and returning an array

A function may receive an array as an argument, process it and return an array result. For example, receive [2,4,6], create a new array by adding 1 to each element, then return [3,5,7]. The caller must use the returned result. Passing the input and returning the output are separate actions; the original changes only if the implementation changes it.

questions.question: What is a parameter?
questions.answer: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.
questions.explanation: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.

questions.question: An urgent fake school message asks a pupil to enter their password through a link. How does phishing exploit users?
options: It systematically guesses every possible password without deceiving a person.
It overwhelms a server only by generating large traffic volumes.
It repairs unsafe user accounts by checking software updates.
Phishing pretends to be a trusted source to trick people into sharing data or doing something unsafe.
questions.answer: D — Phishing pretends to be a trusted source to trick people into sharing data or doing something unsafe.
questions.explanation: It impersonates a trusted source to trick people into revealing data or taking an unsafe action.

questions.question: “Fibre carries electrical signals through copper wire.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Fibre uses light. It supports fast data transfer over long distances and resists electromagnetic interference. Installation can cost more.
questions.explanation: Fibre uses light. It supports fast data transfer over long distances and resists electromagnetic interference. Installation can cost more.

questions.question: Desktops and moving tablets need network links. “Wi-Fi needs a cable from each tablet to the switch.” Correct this. Which links suit these devices?
questions.answer: Ethernet uses cables. Wi-Fi uses radio, so tablets can move around, but interference can affect it. Choose links to suit the distance and data rate needed.
questions.explanation: Ethernet uses cables. Wi-Fi uses radio, so tablets can move around, but interference can affect it. Choose links to suit the distance and data rate needed.

questions.question: Why close a file after use?
questions.answer: It releases the handle or resources and helps ensure buffered writes are completed.
questions.explanation: It releases the handle or resources and helps ensure buffered writes are completed.

questions.question: A wireless keyboard is used close to a computer. When might Bluetooth be suitable?
options: Bluetooth suits short-range links, such as keyboards or headphones. Check range, data rate and power needs.
A high-capacity link between distant sites with no range constraints.
Any intercontinental transfer regardless of distance or required throughput.
Replacing every school's WAN link because short range guarantees high capacity.
questions.answer: A — Bluetooth suits short-range links, such as keyboards or headphones. Check range, data rate and power needs.
questions.explanation: Short-range wireless connections such as a keyboard or headphones, considering bandwidth, range and power needs.
prerequisite_notes: Add Bluetooth suitability; no explicit Bluetooth teaching found in lesson data.

questions.question: “Brute force works only by physically breaking the computer.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It tries many possible passwords or keys until one works.
questions.explanation: It tries many possible passwords or keys until one works.

questions.question: A network shows 2001:db8::7. “IPv6 uses four decimal numbers separated by dots.” Correct this. How is this address written?
questions.answer: IPv6 uses hexadecimal groups separated by colons. Groups of zeros can be shortened. Routers use IP addresses between networks; switches use MAC addresses within a LAN.
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses hexadecimal groups separated by colons. Groups of zeros can be shortened. Routers use IP addresses between networks; switches use MAC addresses within a LAN.

questions.question: What does WHERE do in an SQL query?
questions.answer: It selects rows that meet a condition.
questions.explanation: It selects rows that meet a condition.

questions.question: A LAN switch needs to forward data to interface 02:11:22:33:44:55. What is a MAC address used for and how is it usually written?
options: It is the user's secret password for joining the network.
A MAC address identifies a network interface on a LAN. It is usually six pairs of hexadecimal digits.
It is a website domain used by DNS to identify a web resource.
It is an IPv4 destination written as four decimal numbers.
questions.answer: B — A MAC address identifies a network interface on a LAN. It is usually six pairs of hexadecimal digits.
questions.explanation: It identifies a network interface for local communication, usually as six hexadecimal byte pairs.

questions.question: “A firewall confirms that every sentence on every website is true.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It uses rules to allow or block network traffic.
questions.explanation: It uses rules to allow or block network traffic.

questions.question: Data must reach another network in the right order. “TCP chooses fonts; IP draws images.” Correct this. Explain each protocol's job.
questions.answer: TCP supports reliable delivery in order. IP handles addressing and routing between networks. Each protocol has its own job; encryption does not prove a site is honest.
questions.explanation: TCP supports reliable delivery in order. IP handles addressing and routing between networks. Each protocol has its own job; encryption does not prove a site is honest.

questions.question: Which integers can random(1,6) produce in OCR ERL?
questions.answer: Any integer from 1 through 6 inclusive.
questions.explanation: Any integer from 1 through 6 inclusive.
topics: Generate and use bounded random integers

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) What is HTTP used for? (2) What does HTTPS add to web communication?
options: Web resource transfer / Guarantee of an honest website
Outgoing email only / Guarantee of an honest website
Web resource transfer / Encrypted web communication
Outgoing email only / Encrypted web communication
questions.answer: C — Web resource transfer / Encrypted web communication
questions.explanation: (1) Transferring web resources between web clients and servers. (2) Encrypted communication protects data in transit; it does not prove every site's content is trustworthy.

questions.question: “Penetration testing permits anyone to attack any network without permission.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Testing with permission, within agreed limits, to find and fix security weaknesses.
questions.explanation: Testing with permission, within agreed limits, to find and fix security weaknesses.

questions.question: A zero-indexed 2D array is [[11,12],[21,22]]. Give grid[1,0], then state the indexes needed to access 12.
questions.answer: (a) grid[1,0] is 21; 12 is at grid[0,1].
questions.explanation: (a) grid[1,0] is 21; 12 is at grid[0,1].

questions.question: What does authentication establish?
questions.answer: Whether a user has supplied suitable evidence of the claimed identity.
questions.explanation: Whether a user has supplied suitable evidence of the claimed identity.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair. (1) What is POP usually used for? (2) Why might IMAP suit email on several devices?
options: Send new outgoing mail / Server-based mail synchronisation
Download mail to a client / Outgoing-message delivery only
Send new outgoing mail / Outgoing-message delivery only
Download mail to a client / Server-based mail synchronisation
questions.answer: D — Download mail to a client / Server-based mail synchronisation
questions.explanation: (1) Downloading email from a mail server to a client; local retrieval differs from IMAP synchronisation. (2) It keeps mail on the server and synchronises views and message state across devices.

questions.question: “Changing one protocol layer always requires every other layer to be redesigned.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Layers split communication into tasks. They provide services to each other and help compatibility, development and finding faults.
questions.explanation: Layers split communication into tasks. They provide services to each other and help compatibility, development and finding faults.
prerequisite_notes: Explain benefits of modular layers with a concrete example; the current explanation names stages but does not fully establish the benefits.

questions.question: A drive with private records is lost. “Encryption stops files being stolen or deleted.” Correct this. What does it protect?
questions.answer: Without the key, an attacker cannot easily read ciphertext. Encryption does not stop theft or deletion. Use other controls for other threats.
questions.explanation: Without the key, an attacker cannot easily read ciphertext. Encryption does not stop theft or deletion. Use other controls for other threats.

Sending newly composed email from a client to a mail server.
Synchronising mailbox folders and read state across devices.

questions.explanation: Transferring files between networked computers.

questions.explanation: Malware is made to cause harm, disruption or access without permission. Different types work in different ways.

questions.explanation: A denial-of-service attack floods a service with traffic or requests. Genuine users then cannot use it.

questions.question: For valid ages 13–18, give an ordinary normal test value.
questions.answer: 15 is a representative valid value away from the boundaries.

options: Accessible directly everywhere / Accessible only in one local subprogram
Accessible within local scope / Wider access risks unintended changes
Accessible directly everywhere / Wider access risks unintended changes
Accessible within local scope / Accessible only in one local subprogram
questions.answer: B — Accessible within local scope / Wider access risks unintended changes

questions.answer: Capturing data during transmission, potentially exposing confidential information.
questions.explanation: Capturing data during transmission, potentially exposing confidential information.

questions.question: A new user needs to open and sort files. “A user interface replaces all CPU instructions.” Correct this. How does an interface help?
questions.answer: A user interface lets people use the computer, through GUI controls or typed commands. Other OS tasks manage devices, accounts, memory and files.
questions.explanation: A user interface lets people use the computer, through GUI controls or typed commands. Other OS tasks manage devices, accounts, memory and files.

questions.question: What is the purpose of testing a program against expected outputs?
questions.answer: To compare its actual behaviour with the requirements and identify faults.
questions.explanation: To compare its actual behaviour with the requirements and identify faults.

questions.question: A login application treats user input as part of a query rather than safely handling it as data. What is the concept of SQL injection?
options: An attacker must first know every user's real password.
Merely installing SQL software causes all queries to become malicious.
Unsafe input changes an SQL query. An attacker may then view or change data.
The database has too many valid records and therefore cannot store passwords.
questions.answer: C — Unsafe input changes an SQL query. An attacker may then view or change data.
questions.explanation: Unsafe handling allows malicious input to alter a database query, potentially exposing or changing data.

questions.question: Can an array be passed to or returned from a subprogram?

options: Translate before running; reusable executable / Always create standalone executable first
Retranslate each unchanged statement every run / Always create standalone executable first
Translate before running; reusable executable / Translate and execute during running
Retranslate each unchanged statement every run / Translate and execute during running
questions.answer: C — Translate before running; reusable executable / Translate and execute during running
questions.explanation: (1) It translates the program before execution, producing executable code that can be run again without retranslating unchanged source. (2) It translates and executes during running, usually statement by statement, aiding immediate testing feedback.
